madd_al_lazim.description: Obligatory prolongation over mim sukun — 4 harakat

madd_al_munfasil.description: Permissible prolongation at word boundary with hamza — 4 harakat (2 optional + 2 obligatory)

madd_al_mutasil.description: Obligatory prolongation within word with hamza — 4 harakat

madd_al_arid_lissukun.description: Temporary prolongation before sukun or word ending — 6 harakat (2 optional + 4 obligatory)

madd_al_aarid_lissukun.description: Temporary prolongation before sukun or word ending — 6 harakat (2 optional + 4 obligatory)

madd_al_leen.description: Prolongation on waw/alif followed by sukun — 6 harakat

ghunnah.name: Ghunnah (الغنة)
ghunnah.description: Nasalization emitted when nun or mim carries shadda or sukun. The sound resonates through the nose for 2 harakat.
exercises: Practice sustaining 'nnn' sound with closed mouth for 2 beats after pronouncing 'minhum' and 'mimmā'.
Place finger on nose to feel vibration when pronouncing shadda on ن and م.
Recite سورة الناس slowly, emphasizing the ghunnah on each ن.
ghunnah.explanation_template: Ghunnah requires a nasal resonance of 2 harakat when nun (ن) or mim (م) carries shadda or follows sukun. Your pronunciation at position {position} did not hold the nasal sound for the required duration.

idghaam.name: Idghaam (الإدغام)
idghaam.description: Merging of nun sakinah into the following letter. Six categories exist: idghaam shafawi, idghaam ghunnah, idghaam la ghunnah, idghaam naqis, idghaam kamil, idghaam mutaqaarib.
exercises: Recite phrases ending with ن ساكنة followed by ل or ر — merge without ghunnah.
Practice ين replacing ن + ي in phrases like 'min yadin' → merge with ghunnah.
Practice ون replacing ن + و with sustained nasalization.
idghaam.explanation_template: When nun sakinah (نْ) precedes certain letters, it must merge. For '{target_letter}', the merge {with_without} ghunnah. At position {position}, the nun was pronounced separately instead of being absorbed.

ikhfa.name: Ikhfa (الإخفاء)
ikhfa.description: Concealing the nun sakinah by partially closing the articulation point while maintaining ghunnah, before 15 specific letters.
exercises: Say 'innā anzalnā' — feel the tongue approach the ظ position without fully closing.
Practice 'min thumma' — the ن transitions into the sound of ث with nasal resonance.
Recite سورة القيامة, focusing on concealed ن before each of the 15 ikhfa letters.
ikhfa.explanation_template: Ikhfa requires concealing the نْ by shifting tongue position toward the next letter while maintaining 2-harakat nasalization. At position {position}, the ن before '{target_letter}' was not properly concealed.

iqlab.name: Iqlab (القلب)
iqlab.description: Converting nun sakinah to mim sound when followed by the letter bā (ب), with ghunnah maintained throughout.
exercises: Recite 'inba'ath' — replace نْ with مْ sound before ب.
Practice سورة المطففين: 'أن betūm' — feel the ن → م transition.
Exaggerate the bilabial closure: hold the م sound for 2 beats before releasing into ب.
iqlab.explanation_template: When نْ is followed by ب (bā), it converts to a م sound (iqlab). At position {position}, the ن before ب was pronounced as ن rather than being converted to م.

qalqalah.name: Qalqalah (القلقلة)
qalqalah.description: An echo or bouncing sound produced when bā, jīm, dāl, ṭā, or qāf carry sukun — the sound reverberates at the point of articulation.
exercises: Say 'qāl' — feel the qāf bounce when released from sukun.
Practice 'bad', 'jadd', 'ṭalq', 'qadd' — emphasize the echo on each release.
Recite أ擢د الله العظيم repeatedly, feeling each qalqalah letter snap.
qalqalah.explanation_template: Qalqalah letters (ب, ج, د, ط, ق) produce a bouncing echo when carrying sukun. At position {position}, the letter '{letter}' was pronounced flatly without the required reverberation.

madd_al_tabi_i.name: Madd al-Tabi'i (المد الطبيعي)
madd_al_tabi_i.description: Natural prolongation of 2 harakat required when a long vowel letter (alif, waw, ya) is followed by hamza.
exercises: Count 'aa' for 2 beats: 'qā-a-la', 'nū-u-run', 'khay-yi-run'.
Recite سورة الفاتحة slowly: 'ā-meen' with full 2-beat elongation.
Use a metronome at 120 bpm: each long vowel gets exactly 2 clicks.
madd_al_tabi_i.explanation_template: Long vowels followed by hamza require 2 harakat of prolongation. At position {position}, the vowel '{vowel}' was held for {actual} harakat instead of the required 2.

madd_al_munfasil.name: Madd al-Munfasil (المد المنفصل)
madd_al_munfasil.description: Prolongation at a word boundary where a long vowel meets hamza across two words. Minimum 2 harakat, recommended 4 (2 optional + 2 obligatory).
exercises: Recite 'alā an' — hold the ā across the word boundary for 4 harakat.
Practice 'ar-rūḥu ilā' — count 4 beats across the pause.
Distinguish from madd al-mutasil: this split occurs BETWEEN words, not within one.
madd_al_munfasil.explanation_template: At word boundaries, if a long vowel meets hamza across words, at least 4 harakat are recommended. At position {position}, the prolongation was only {actual} harakat.

madd_al_mutasil.name: Madd al-Mutasil (المد المتصل)
madd_al_mutasil.description: Obligatory 4-harakat prolongation when a long vowel letter is followed by hamza WITHIN the same word.
exercises: Say 'sū-a' — hold the ū for 4 beats before the hamza.
Recite 'mu'tamir' — the wāw-madd to hamza must be 4 harakat.
Practice all madd al-mutasil words in سورة النور for repetition.
madd_al_mutasil.explanation_template: Within a word, when a madd letter precedes hamza, 4 harakat are obligatory. At position {position}, the vowel '{vowel}' was held for {actual} harakat instead of 4.

madd_al_aarid_lissukun.name: Madd al-'Aarid li-l-Sukun (المد العارض للسكون)
madd_al_aarid_lissukun.description: Temporary prolongation of 6 harakat when a long vowel is followed by sukun (temporary stop). 2 harakat are the vowel's natural length + 4 optional.
exercises: Recite 'an-nas' with a pause: the ā in 'an-' stretches to 6 harakat at the stop.
Practice this only when stopping: reciting continuously, the vowel reverts to 2 harakat.
Compare stopping vs continuous: 'ar-Raḥmān[stop]' vs 'ar-Raḥmānī'.
madd_al_aarid_lissukun.explanation_template: When stopping at a sukun, the preceding long vowel extends to 6 harakat. At position {position}, the vowel before the stop was only {actual} harakat.

waqf_ibtida.name: Waqf & Ibtida (الوقف والابتداء)
waqf_ibtida.description: Rules for stopping (waqf) and restarting (ibtida) recitation — proper pronunciation at pause points including mandatory stops, optional stops, and mandatory continuation signs.
exercises: Learn the stop symbols: مـ (must stop), جـ (permissible), صـ (beautiful stop), لا (no stop).
Practice stopping on مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّين — release the final dīn with ghunnah, not with idghaam.
When restarting after a stop ending in sukun, re-pronounce the hamzahWasl or keep the pause silent.
waqf_ibtida.explanation_template: At position {position}, the pause/start rule ({waqf_type}) was not observed correctly. {detail}
